From the moment you walk in, it genuinely feels like you’ve stepped out of Bombay and into a beautifully curated space somewhere down South. The interiors are warm, aesthetic, and incredibly inviting — think soft yellow table lamps, subtle detailing, and the gentle fragrance of fresh mogra flowers placed on your table that instantly elevate the entire dining experience.

Coming to the food — easily some of the most incredible South Indian cuisine I’ve had. Everything feels authentic, rich, and thoughtfully put together.

My absolute favourites (and honestly, you cannot go wrong with this order):

> Railway curry with Malabar parotta — deeply flavourful, comforting, and indulgent in the best way
> Jackfruit cutlets — crispy outside, soft and packed with flavour inside
> Ghee podi idli — simple, yet executed so perfectly that it becomes unforgettable

One of the most special touches here is something you don’t even have to order — they complimentary bring you a curry tasting spread. It’s their way of introducing you to the menu, where you get to sample a variety of curries like sambar, rasam, coconut-based gravies, paired with different rice options like coconut rice, tamarind rice and more. It feels less like a service and more like a warm, thoughtful gesture — guiding you through the flavours before you even decide what to order.

Now let’s talk about the cocktails — because wow.
These are hands down some of the best cocktails I’ve had. They’re dangerously good — so well-balanced and delicious that you don’t even realise how strong they are until they hit you. Every single time.

The service ties everything together — attentive, warm, and genuinely invested in making sure you have a great time.

Overall, this place nails everything — food, vibe, ambience, drinks, and even pricing for the experience it offers.

A solid 9.5/10 — and an absolute must-visit if you want to indulge in South Indian cuisine like never before.

The non-veg starters were a major highlight—the Mutton Cutlets, Prawn Fry, and Chicken 65 were all intensely flavored, succulent, and perfectly spiced.For the mains, we ordered the legendary Mutton Madras Railway Curry paired with soft, lacy Appams and flaky, layered Malabar Parottas. The richness of the slow-cooked gravy paired beautifully with the breads. We also tried the Chicken Kothu Parotta, which delivered that authentic, robust street-food punch.We wrapped up the massive feast with three distinct types of payasam, which provided a wonderfully comforting, sweet finale to our meal.Beyond the food, the lush, green outdoor ambiance is gorgeous and creates a deeply relaxing environment. The hospitality was top-notch. Highly recommended for anyone craving upscale, homestyle South Indian cuisine in Goregaon!

featured_reviews.name: Suyog Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room, Nesco (Gate 2) – A Worthwhile Bucket List Experience!

I finally visited The Tanjore Tiffin Room at the Nesco compound (near Gate 2) on the last day of 2025, and it truly lived up to the expectations. I had pre-booked through the District app (which gave ~₹500 off), and despite peak-hour crowds around 2:30 PM, we were seated immediately. Valet parking is available, which is convenient.
The menu is limited to south indian cuisine but well-curated. We started with Kotthu Parrota and Karaikudi Prawns marinated with curry leaves & raw mango, along with Peach Iced Tea and a Virgin Mojito. Before ordering mains, the staff offered a curry sampler—a great touch where they explained and let us taste gravies like Stew, Chettinad, etc. Everything tasted rich, flavourful, and authentic.
For mains, we chose the Chicken Stew (a mild, coconut-milk based gravy) paired with Appam, Egg Appam, and Set Dosa. Despite the rush, dishes arrived surprisingly fast. The ambience was calming, lighting and seating were comfortable, and the place has a very warm, rooted vibe. Staff was friendly, polite, and attentive throughout.
A lovely gesture—Yelanki bananas served with the bill—felt like a thoughtful nod to tradition.
Overall: A memorable experience with great flavours, excellent service, and strong cultural touchpoints. A bit on the expensive side, but worth it for a special outing.

featured_reviews.name: Pratiksha Jagger
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our meal began on a plateau with standard appetizers and drinks that felt a bit lackluster—I’ve definitely had better Chicken 65 and Mutton Pepper Fry elsewhere. But then, the "curry tray" arrived. The waiter walked us through a tasting of every sauce available, which was an incredible touch. We opted for the Chicken Stew and Madras Railway Curry with Mutton and Malabar Parotta; both were phenomenal and packed with flavor. The main course was the undisputed star of the show.
Pro tip: Skip the starters and save all your room for the mains!

featured_reviews.name: Buddy Caprice
featured_reviews.review_text: The place clearly is Insta-worthy and food is amazing too! It's conveniently located inside NESCO from Gate no. 2 and has tons of waiting people there so pre-book your tables before going. Do not forget to first ask them to get the Tasting plate where they share a variety of curries, chutneys and rice options in small bowls to help you taste before you order. They serve veg and non veg and seafood options with the gravy you select from this plate. They have a great A-la-carte menu too and food tastes great. We tried their Egg Bonda and Jackfruit cutlets which were unique in taste but deliciously paired with a delectable chutney. We then ordered Appams with white vegetable gravy which were lip smackingly good and lemon rice which tasted awesome without any dal/gravy needed. We also tried some of their cocktails and mocktails which were great too. The entrance is definately worth a click and for memories while the hip music at a lower volume does offer space for conversations across the table. Their outdoor seating is a little cramped but nonetheless beautifully decorated with vintage chandeliers and authentic bronze lamp setup. The indoor seating is cozy and the green beige white combination bring about a certain vibe. Great for families, colleagues, teams and groups of friends but also ideal for a date night! Must visit during the evenings when the lighting is amazingly calm. For two, we paid around 3000₹ and tried everything from a starter to drinks to main course and dessert! Recommend this outlet and the one at Versova too. Been to both and have not been disappointed!

featured_reviews.name: DIANA JEROME
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited three times at three completely different hours — 11:47 AM, 8:00 PM, and 10:00 PM. Every single time, the staff came up with the same ridiculous excuse that the AC room was "not open." How are we supposed to believe that when we could clearly see people already sitting inside and enjoying the air-conditioned seating?

This is nothing but poor management and dishonest behavior. The outside seating is unbearably hot, and a few tall fans are nowhere near enough to make it comfortable. If you have an AC room in the basement, then what is the point of having it if regular customers are constantly denied access to it?

The food is good, but good food cannot make up for such pathetic service. The staff seems more interested in making excuses than helping customers. Three visits, three different times, and the exact same nonsense every time. This was extremely frustrating and disrespectful. If you cannot provide the facilities you advertise, then be honest about it instead of wasting customers' time.

Very disappointing experience. Good food, terrible service, and absolutely no regard for customer comfort.

featured_reviews.name: Aiman Behlim
featured_reviews.review_text: Idli Dosafusion serves a delicious and satisfying South Indian breakfast. The ghee-roasted dosa with bullet powder, paired with fresh sambar and coconut chutney 🥥on a banana leaf, along with a cup of filter coffee☕️is my go-to choice. The masala idli and Mysore dosa are also must-tries. The ambience is decent, though cleanliness could be improved. Service is satisfactory but has room for enhancement. The menu display on the TV is a nice touch. Overall, the food is fresh, flavorful, and definitely worth the money.

featured_reviews.name: Praphul S Sreedhar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place for some dosa cravings, and here’s my take:

Masala Dosa – Crispy, golden, and really delicious. The masala filling is flavorful and well-balanced. However, the size is on the smaller side for the price (₹120).

Sada Dosa – Equally crispy and tasty, with that perfect fermented batter aroma. Again, size feels small for the price (₹100).

While the taste is impressive, a single dosa here isn’t enough to satisfy a big appetite (I could easily have two) ☺️

Great flavors and crispiness that make you want more, but be ready to pay a premium for smaller portions. Price is little high
